Atlantis AI for NDT Defect Detection 2027 — Machine Learning Models with Level III Approval

Atlantis AI for NDT delivers machine learning defect detection for phased-array UT (PAUT), radiographic testing (RT), conventional ultrasonic testing (UT), and time-of-flight diffraction (TOFD). Code-Acceptance Pathway — ASME V Article 1 + API 510/570/653

The code-acceptance question for AI-assisted NDE: does ASME V Article 1 "personnel capable of performing the examination" extend to AI-augmented acquisition + interpretation? Industry consensus (ASME Section V Subgroup on Computed Imaging + API Committee on Refinery Equipment + IACS Rec-20) — yes, when: (a) procedure written + qualified + Level III approved; (b) AI model validated per a repeatable, reproducible, documented framework (ASTM E2491 + ASME PCC-3 + API 581 inspection-effectiveness factor); (c) acquisition operator trained per applicable inspector scheme; (d) human-in-the-loop Level III final disposition. Atlantis AI delivers the full code-acceptance documentation package out-of-box.

Method Coverage — PAUT + RT + UT + TOFD

Phased-array UT (PAUT) — defect classification (crack, slag, porosity, lack-of-fusion) + sizing per Sector + S-scan + E-scan + Sectorial-scan data. Radiographic testing (RT) — defect classification on digital DR + CR + film-digitised images, IQI verification, geometric distortion correction. Conventional UT — defect amplitude + dynamic-echo analysis on A-scan + B-scan + C-scan + D-scan data. TOFD — defect-tip diffraction + through-wall sizing per ASTM E2373.

Model Validation Framework — ASTM E2491 + ASME PCC-3

Atlantis AI model validation: (1) Training data provenance — every training image / scan tagged with operator + date + equipment + reference standard + ground-truth disposition; (2) Cross-validated K-fold on hold-out sets per damage-mechanism class; (3) Reproducibility — same input → same output across runs; (4) Robustness — synthetic perturbation testing (noise, scaling, rotation); (5) Bias testing — performance parity across geometry, weld config, material grade, scanner make/model; (6) ASME PCC-3 inspection-effectiveness factor — AI-assisted vs Level II human baseline.

Vertical Use Cases — Refining + Marine + Aerospace + Power + LNG

Refining: weld inspection on heater coils, reactor effluent piping, sour-service pressure vessels. Marine: weld inspection on FPSO topside + jacket + hull during drydock, classification-society IACS Rec-20 acceptance. Aerospace: fastener-hole inspection on aging aircraft lap-joint, composite layup verification, gas turbine disc + blade NDE. Power: HP/HT steam header inspection, HRSG tube inspection, condenser tube inspection. LNG: cryogenic-service pressure vessel + storage tank inspection. Offshore wind: monopile + jacket weld inspection during installation + IRM.

Human-in-the-Loop Workflow with Level III Sign-Off

Workflow: (1) inspector acquires data per qualified procedure; (2) Atlantis AI runs first-pass interpretation — defect classification + sizing + acceptance recommendation per code; (3) inspector reviews + accepts or overrides AI; (4) Level III reviews any AI override + any AI-classified critical defect + signs off final disposition; (5) audit-trail records every step — inspector ID, AI confidence score, AI rationale, override reason, Level III signature. Atlantis AI never deploys in "autonomous" mode — always human-decided.
